description: A stereo memory effect: a write head runs endlessly round a buffer, a map is kept of where real sound is, and fragments are recalled from it, each return a little more worn than the last

params.text: Sets how far back the recall engine may reach, 50ms to the whole buffer
Sets how often and how likely an automatic recall is; at the bottom of its travel only the event button and jack recall anything
Sets how hard a recalled fragment deteriorates: the interpolation coarsens, the top end goes, the sample rate and bit depth drop, the timing jitters, and at the top dropouts appear
Turns distinct fragments into a diffuse, slowly modulated allpass cloud with stereo crossfeed, from discrete repeats up to something close to reverb
Sets how long stored regions keep their integrity: low lets a region be recalled many times, high makes it fade as the write head passes over it and be avoided after fewer replays
Sets how unstable the behaviour is: per-fragment jitter in position and pitch, spatial drift, and a scattering of the recall timing by up to seventy per cent either way
Sets how likely a recalled fragment is to play backwards; it is chosen afresh for each recollection rather than crossfaded
Crossfades the dry and treated signals at equal power
Sets the final output level, unity at noon
Sets how far a recalled fragment's pitch may stray: unisons and octaves at the bottom of its travel, then fifths and fourths, then thirds, then the full chromatic set
Chooses when memories return: a window round a region's strongest block fired by transients, a rate following the input's envelope, or a rate rising as the input falls quiet
Chooses what the present does to what is already stored: Oblivion replaces it, Remanence rewrites it but leaves traces, and Sediment accumulates on top of it through a saturator and a DC blocker
Stops the write head, while recollection, feedback and deterioration all keep running; the transport keeps advancing so the timing stays consistent when it is let go
Forces a recall from a valid region
Wipes the buffer, the activity map, the region descriptors, the playback heads and the feedback
Chooses what the recall engine reads: the dry input, the mix, or the wet recollections themselves, which makes the recalls self-triggering
Sets how much of the wet output is fed back into what is written, from none through regeneration and past unity into self-oscillation, bounded by a saturator and a limiter

inputs.text: The left side of the signal to store
The right side of the signal to store; with nothing patched here the left jack feeds both sides
Above its threshold the write head is stopped; the menu chooses whether it is a gate, a toggle, or a toggle on the rising edge
A rising edge forces a recall from a valid region
A rising edge wipes the buffer and everything derived from it
Added to the memory knob, ±5V for about half its travel
Added to the recall knob, ±5V for about half its travel
Added to the age knob, ±5V for about half its travel
Added to the smear knob, ±5V for about half its travel
Added to the forget knob, ±5V for about half its travel
Added to the temper knob, ±5V for about half its travel
Added to the direction knob, ±5V for about half its travel
Added to the mix knob, ±5V for about half its travel
Added to the out knob, ±5V for about half its travel
Added to the harmony knob, ±5V for about half its travel

outputs.text: The left side of the treated signal
The right side of the treated signal
The recalled material before the smear, the feedback and the mix, for treating in parallel or feeding back by another path
A short 10V pulse whenever a recollection actually begins
The envelope of whatever the src switch has the recall engine reading, 0V to 10V
A slow voltage from the module's own state, the mean age of the active regions blended with the activity at the write head; the menu makes it stepped or smooth and bipolar or unipolar

notes: that switch prints its three settings in the order those three behaviours are described.
the recall engine only ever picks regions the activity map says contain sound, so it never recalls silence.
the strip across the top is a view of the buffer: yellow bars are the energy in each block, a moving line is the write head, and the panel flashes on each recollection.
with the src switch on wet and the fb trimmer high the module becomes a drone generator that sustains itself with nothing patched in.
menu: Quality — how many region descriptors are kept: Eco (4 descriptors), Standard (8) or High (16)
Buffer size — how long the buffer is: 4 s, 8 s, 16 s or 32 s
Remanence retention — how much of the old material survives a pass in the remanence memory mode: 10%, 30%, 50% or 70%
Sediment input amount — how hard the present is added on top in the sediment memory mode: 0.5x, 1.0x, 1.5x or 2.0x
Sediment saturation — the shape the sediment mode saturates with: Soft, Tape or Fold
Temper scatters recall timing — on by default; switched off, the recall clock stays regular however far temper is turned up
Freeze behavior — how the freeze button and jack act: Gate, Toggle, or Toggle on rising edge
Mono output — Stereo, Left only, Stereo sum or Equal-power sum
Random seed — Random on load, or Fixed so a patch always behaves the same way
Reseed now — rolls a new seed at once
Chaos out: stepped — holds the chaos output at a value between updates rather than sliding
Chaos out: bipolar — puts the chaos output at ±5V rather than 0V to 10V
